notes: Universities of Excellence, list in force today (2026-10-12): the first-period list decided 19 July 2019 (10 universities + 1 alliance = 11 funding cases, not 11 universities + 1 alliance). Funding began 1 November 2019 and runs to December 2026 (GWK: 'November 2019 bis Dezember 2026'; the WR call text originally named 31 October 2026 as end).

Newly decided list (in force from 1 January 2027, 7-year period 2027-2033, permanent funding subject to evaluation every 7 years): 15 funding cases = 12 universities + 3 alliances (20 universities in 17 cities). 10 continued by the Excellence Commission on 11 March 2026; 5 new selected on 2 October 2026 from 11 applications.

Universität Konstanz is not continued from 2027 (it no longer has the required minimum number of Clusters of Excellence). WR page mentions degressive phase-out funding for up to three years for sites that leave; exact Konstanz arrangement not verified.

Unsuccessful 2026 new applicants (from the DFG/WR list of 11 March 2026): Northwest Alliance (Universität Bremen, Carl von Ossietzky Universität Oldenburg), H_CORE (Justus-Liebig-Universität Gießen, Philipps-Universität Marburg), Leibniz Universität Hannover, Medizinische Hochschule Hannover, Christian-Albrechts-Universität zu Kiel, Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg.

Berlin University Alliance: official DFG/WR lists name only FU, HU and TU Berlin; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin is listed as a member on exzellenzstrategie.de and in 2019 announcements. All four are in Berlin.

Clusters: complete list of 70 transcribed from the official DFG/WR PDF (German and English versions) of the 22 May 2025 Excellence Commission meeting; funding 1 January 2026 for 7 years (2026-2032). Cross-checked: exzellenzstrategie.de shows exactly the same 70 tagged 'Förderphase 2026-2032'; 45 continuations + 25 new; 43 universities (37 municipalities, 13 Länder) - all matching the DFG press release.

Cluster acronyms: taken from the official titles or from the exzellenzstrategie.de short labels (e.g. RAI, REC², DYNAVERSE, CECAD, IntCDC, In_equality). null where no acronym is used officially; 'shortName' gives the portal label. Commonly used informal acronyms (e.g. 'FSC' for the Fuel Science Center, 'TAM' for The Adaptive Mind) are NOT given because they are not in the official lists.
e-conversion 2.0: the portal still shows the old German subtitle 'e-conversion – Energie verstehen an den Grenzflächen'; the official 2025 list title is just 'e-conversion 2.0'.

Source inconsistencies: (a) GWK page says the evaluation decision was on 26 March 2026; DFG/WR press release and list say 11 March 2026 (used). (b) WR Exzellenzstrategie page says 'Seit Januar 2026 werden 40 Cluster an 43 deutschen Universitäten gefördert' - evidently a typo for 70. (c) DFG programme page still mentions 'bis zu maximal 4 neue Förderfälle' while the press release states 5 were selected (up to 5 were allowed per WR/GWK). (d) exzellenzstrategie.de Universities listing labels the first period '2020-2026' and had not yet added the 5 new sites at retrieval.

Coordinates: approximate (main building / main campus) from Wikidata P625, rounded to 4 decimals; not checked against official campus addresses. Overrides: KIT -> Campus Süd (the KIT item points to Campus Nord in Eggenstein-Leopoldshafen); Halle -> Löwengebäude; Leipzig -> Augusteum (university items lack coordinates).

Municipality caveats for puzzle use: Universität Hohenheim is in Stuttgart (same municipality as Universität Stuttgart); Technische Universität Hamburg is in Hamburg-Harburg; FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg assigned to Erlangen (also large sites in Nürnberg); Martin-Luther-Universität Halle-Wittenberg assigned to Halle (Saale); TUM main site in München (big campuses in Garching and Freising); Universität Stuttgart point is Campus Stadtmitte (main campus Vaihingen also in Stuttgart).
City names are German municipality names; GeoNames short names may differ (e.g. 'Freiburg' vs 'Freiburg im Breisgau', 'Halle' vs 'Halle (Saale)', 'Frankfurt' vs 'Frankfurt am Main').
